original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: Does one root-axis query still fit 2^{4 ell}(p+2)^{16} when four rotation networks are compiled by the PR #4192 shared-arena scan, after the one-axis CRT bill is included, for every integer p >= 2 and 1 <= h <= ell <= p?
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one quantified implication of #4100 at its caller. research/crt-uniform-evaluator already proves the per-table constant C=1 and leaves the shared-arena schedule open. This package takes that schedule for one root axis, including the four networks that axis builds and the one-axis CRT bill.
bottleneck_link: PR #4100 pays E(p, ell) inside the CRT route. An explicit arena schedule that still fits that same E for one axis keeps the constant available for the scan PR #4192 describes. It does not select a new exponent. The same per-action charge does not fit all 8(p+2) axes at once.
stop_rule: Stop after the one-axis four-network inequality and the explicit 8(p+2)-axis counterexample under the same charge. Do not price reservoir placement, the ordinary callee, or a new kappa.
evidence: PROOF.md derives U <= 2^{4 ell}(p+2)^{16} for one axis and four arena networks, and shows the 32-axis bill at p=2, ell=2 exceeds that allowance. verify.py checks the inductions, source sentences, corner witnesses and the batch excess. It prints PASS_CRT_ARENA_ROOT_AXIS.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance with the proof, verifier and package text.

open_questions.question: Does a word-level scalar inventory, with a fixed number of w-bit operations per arena record, bring all 8(p+2) axes inside 2^{4 ell}(p+2)^{16}?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The schoolbook-per-tape-action majorant fits one axis and exceeds the allowance on the full displayed batch at p=2, ell=2. A tighter inventory could change that batch comparison without changing the one-axis theorem.
open_questions.first_step: Replace 8 w^2 per tape action by the per-record comparisons in PR #4192 section 2 and compare the 8(p+2)-axis bill with 2^{4 ell}(p+2)^{16}.
open_questions.blocked_by: That tighter inventory is not proved in this package. The theorem uses one schoolbook product per tape action.

open_questions.question: With one arena axis inside E, do the reservoir placement and ordinary interchange callee of CRT.md sections 3-4 still fit their stated bills?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The evaluator constant is one factor in the CRT route. Placement and the callee can reintroduce an E-sized term.
open_questions.first_step: Check H >= G at G = 64(ell + ceil(log2(p+2))) on the size family in #4100, using C=1 for this one-axis arena bill.
open_questions.blocked_by: Placement geometry is PR #4174 and is not an input to this arena bill.
